author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Manchester completed its first month without a suspected overdose fatality since 2015, according to a report from American Medical Response announced by the city.

The city described the result as the first such month in 140 months. Officials credited coordinated work by emergency medical crews, police, firefighters, public-health teams, treatment providers and recovery organizations, while emphasizing that the opioid crisis remains an active threat.

The milestone concerns suspected overdose deaths reported for the month, not a declaration that the crisis is over or that all cases have completed final review. A single month also does not establish a lasting trend. Even so, the absence of a suspected fatality marks a notable break from more than a decade of continuous loss.

Manchester said continued prevention, rapid response and recovery support remain necessary. The city directed people seeking substance-use treatment to New Hampshire’s Doorway program through 211 and reminded residents to call 911 for a suspected overdose. Future monthly data will show whether the improvement is sustained.
dek: American Medical Response reported that Manchester completed its first month in 140 months without a suspected overdose fatality.
headline: Manchester records first month without a suspected overdose death since 2015
